sections.html:
Tulsa County covers 587 square miles in northeast Oklahoma, with Tulsa as the county seat and largest city. Cities wholly or partly inside it include Bixby, Broken Arrow, Collinsville, Glenpool, Jenks, Owasso, Sand Springs, Sapulpa, Skiatook and Tulsa, plus the towns of Liberty, Lotsee and Sperry. The city your house sits in affects permits and school boundaries, so name the city whenever you ask a county office about an address.

The 2020 census counted 669,279 people and 292,375 housing units, with 8.7% vacant. Owners occupy 57.9% of occupied homes and renters 42.1%. With about 42% of homes rented, many county properties are rentals, and landlords should check whose name the assessor shows as of January 1.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a home
sections.html:
Each January 1 the assessor assigns a Fair Cash (Market) Value, drawing on sales from the prior 24 months. The office weighs location, size, build quality, condition and age, and every residential parcel gets a fresh value yearly.

Your notice lists three figures. Fair Cash Value is the market guess. Taxable Fair Cash Value is what the tax is calculated from; it may climb no more than 3% a year under a homestead exemption or agricultural use, or 5% on other real property, unless a transfer or improvement is added. Assessed Value (Gross) is now 11% of the taxable figure.

A purchase lifts the cap, so a buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Long-time owners often carry a taxable value far under market.

Step one is an informal protest with the assessor. Unhappy with the result? Take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization, and after that to District Court.

  • The owner of record on January 1 may protest, as may a representative holding written authorization.
  • The window is 30 calendar days from the date printed on the Notice of Valuation, or up to the first Monday in April when your value stayed the same.
  • Send forms by mail, bring them in, or email informalprotest@tulsacounty.org. Phone hearings are available.
  • Photos, independent appraisals and repair estimates strengthen a case. Sales after January 1 of the current year do not count.

Notices are mailed only when the market or taxable value goes up, so no notice means your value stayed flat or fell. Report storm, flood or fire damage to the assessor at 918-596-5100 and include any insurance or fire marshal report.

Six kinds of relief exist: homestead, additional homestead, the senior valuation limitation, the circuit breaker refund, the 100% disabled veteran exemption and religious or charitable exemptions. Four matter most to a typical homeowner.

  • Homestead: takes $1,000 off the assessed valuation of a primary residence. To count this year, file by March 15 or within 30 days of the valuation notice date.
  • Additional homestead: a second $1,000 for homestead owners whose gross household income is $30,000 or less (effective January 1, 2024). Under age 65, you must refile yearly.
  • Senior valuation limitation: freezes taxable value for owners 65 and older who qualify for homestead and fall under the HUD income limit.
  • Circuit breaker (538-H): a refund for qualifying low-income owners, capped at $200, with claims due to the Oklahoma Tax Commission by June 30.

File with the assessor's Taxpayer Services office on the 5th floor of the county headquarters, 218 W. Sixth Street, or online.

Pay the Treasurer at 218 W. 6th Street, 8th Floor, in Tulsa, or by mail, phone or the county's tax roll site. Half is due ahead of January 1 and the other half ahead of April 1. A bill of $25 or less is due whole before January 1. Late payments add interest, costs and fees.

  • Credit card: 2.35%, with a $1.95 minimum.
  • Debit card: 1.95%.
  • Electronic check: $1.75, up to $100,000.

The payment processor charges those fees, not the county. The Treasurer warns that Doxo.com is not affiliated with the office and should not be used for property tax. Statements go out in November, and remote bank collection sites open for three weeks after Thanksgiving.

The county never prorates tax when a house sells. When tax is still owed, the title company can take a share from each side and forward it. When the year's tax is not certified yet and nothing is owing, the buyer normally receives a closing credit for your share and pays the whole bill later.

Unpaid property tax is settled from your sale proceeds by the title company, so a balance does not have to be cleared before you take an offer.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the June auction
sections.html:
Tax left unpaid can send a property to the Treasurer's real estate auction on the second Monday of June; next one is June 14, 2027. A typical year sees 475 to 500 properties sold over unpaid taxes or special assessments like cleaning and mowing.

MonthTreasurer mailing or action
NovemberOriginal tax statements, with a second resale notice if a property is scheduled for auction
JanuaryNew owner and first delinquent statements
MarchFinal notification of tax resale
MayResale publication and land list
JuneJune resale auction
JulyUnsold properties move to the Commissioners' sale list

A statute change effective November 1, 2025 means a property comes off the auction list only if paid before bidding opens. The deadline is 5:00 p.m. on June 11, 2027. Lots that draw no buyer turn into county property, available through the Commissioners' sale process.

Owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled may be exempt from tax resale if they live in a single-family home that is not a rental, earn under the federal income guidelines, and hold an assessor value of $180,000 or less. Apply before each year's resale.

sections.h2: Title and records to check before listing
sections.html:
Deeds and death certificates are recorded with the Tulsa County Clerk, and the assessor updates its records from what the clerk receives. If the assessor shows the wrong owner, the usual causes are an unrecorded deed, an error on a recorded deed, or a lot split that will not show until the next year's roll.

  • A surviving joint tenant on a deed with a right of survivorship clause can file an affidavit with a certified death certificate. Without that clause, talk to an attorney.
  • To split or combine lots inside Tulsa or the unincorporated county, call INCOG at 918-584-7526. Other cities have their own planning offices.
  • A manufactured home sale or move needs an OTC 936 form from the assessor.
  • A parcel is taxed as it existed on January 1, so a lot you sold in part after that date still produces a bill for the whole parcel.

Clear these before listing. Each unresolved item adds time at the title company.

Owing tax does not rule out a quick sale. We pull the Treasurer's record, view the house and write up an offer that already counts the tax and any liens paid at closing. Set it beside the figures for listing. Declining costs you nothing.

faqs.q: When are Tulsa County property taxes due?
faqs.a: At least half must be paid before January 1, and the second half before April 1. Taxes of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1. Late payments bring interest, costs and fees.

faqs.q: Does Tulsa County prorate taxes when a house sells?
faqs.a: No. The county bills the full year, and the closing company usually divides it between buyer and seller on the closing statement.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Tulsa County value?
faqs.a: File an informal protest with the Assessor within 30 calendar days of the valuation notice, or by the first Monday in April if your value did not change. Call 918-596-5100 or email informalprotest@tulsacounty.org.

faqs.q: What is the Tulsa County tax auction date for 2027?
faqs.a: June 14, 2027, the second Monday of June. Payment to remove a property must be made before the auction starts, with a 5:00 p.m. cutoff on June 11, 2027.

faqs.q: When do I file for the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Applications are accepted all year, but to count for the current year they must be filed by March 15 or within 30 days of the date on the valuation notice. Later filings take effect the following year.
